name: RT Auction Product for WooCommerce – Online Auction & Bidding
author: raintech357

sections.description:
Want to sell products to the highest bidder? RT Auction Product for WooCommerce lets you run online auctions right inside your existing WooCommerce store. No new website, no extra software, and no coding needed.

Add an “Auction” product just like any other product. Choose when it starts, when it ends, and the starting price. Your customers place bids, watch the countdown, and the winner pays through your normal WooCommerce checkout.

It works for collectibles, art, antiques, used equipment, charity fundraisers, limited-edition items, clearance stock, and anything else you want to sell to the highest bidder.

Why store owners love it

  • Easy to set up. Create an auction in about a minute from the product page.
  • Feels live. Prices, bids and the countdown timer update on the page by themselves. Customers never need to refresh.
  • Fair for everyone. Two people bidding at the same moment never causes mix-ups.
  • Less chasing. The winner is emailed automatically and pays through your normal checkout.
  • Works with your theme and payment methods. Winners pay with the same payment options you already use.

Everything you need to run great auctions

Ways to sell

  • Standard auctions. Everyone sees the current price and bids openly.
  • Automatic bidding (proxy bidding). A bidder enters the most they will pay. The plugin bids for them, one small step at a time, only as much as needed to stay in front. Their top amount stays private.
  • Sealed-bid auctions. Nobody can see the bids until the auction ends. The highest bid wins.
  • Buy It Now. Let shoppers skip the bidding and buy straight away at a fixed price. You can switch it off as soon as the first bid comes in.

Protect your price

  • Reserve price. Set a secret minimum. If bidding ends below it, you are not forced to sell. Bidders only see “reserve met” or “reserve not met”.
  • Starting price. Choose where the bidding begins.
  • Bid steps. Choose how much each new bid must go up by, or set different steps for different price levels (for example, steps of 1 up to 100, then steps of 5).
  • Last-minute protection. If someone bids right before the end, the auction is extended a few minutes so others get a fair chance to respond.
  • Buyer’s fee. Add a percentage fee for the winner, the way traditional auction houses do.

Save yourself time

  • Automatic relisting. Unsold items can go back up for auction by themselves, as many times as you choose.
  • Second chance offers. If the winner never pays, offer the item to the next-highest bidder with one click.
  • Payment deadline. Winners get a set number of days to pay. After that, you are told so you can act.
  • One-click relist and end early. Start over or finish an auction whenever you like.

Keep bidders coming back

  • Watchlist. Shoppers save auctions they like and get a reminder before they end.
  • Email alerts. Bidders are told when they are outbid, when they win, and when an auction they follow is about to end.
  • “People watching” counter. Show how much interest an item has.
  • My Account page. Customers see their active bids, their wins and their watchlist in one place.
  • Auction lists on any page. Show live, upcoming or ended auctions anywhere with a simple shortcode.

Stay in control

  • Dashboard. See live auctions, total bids, sales and revenue, a chart of recent bidding activity, auctions ending soon, and anything that needs your attention.
  • Auction list. Search and filter all your auctions, see who is winning, and manage each one.
  • Bidder management. See who is bidding and block anyone who causes problems.
  • Spam protection. Keep brand-new accounts from bidding until they are a few days old.
  • Privacy for bidders. Hide full names in the public bid list (for example “j***n”).
  • Bid records. Review every bid and download them as a spreadsheet file.
  • Email alerts for you. Get notified when an auction ends, when a winner pays, and, if you like, when each bid comes in.

Simple shortcode

Show your auctions anywhere with:

[rtapw_auctions status="live" limit="12" columns="3"]

Use status="upcoming" or status="ended" for other lists. Sort by ending time, newest, or price.

Great for

  • Online auctions for art, antiques and collectibles
  • Charity and fundraising auctions
  • Selling used or refurbished goods to the highest bidder
  • Limited-edition and rare product drops
  • Clearing out surplus stock
sections.installation:
1. Go to Plugins > Add New and search for “RT Auction Product for WooCommerce”, then click Install Now, or upload the plugin zip file.
  2. Click Activate. (WooCommerce must already be installed and active.)
  3. Go to Products > Add New and set the product type to Auction.
  4. Open the Auction tab, set your starting price, bid step and end date, then publish.
  5. Visit Auctions > Settings to choose your emails, payment deadline and other options.

That’s it. Your auction is live.
sections.faq:
How do I create an auction in WooCommerce?

Add a new product and change the product type to “Auction”. In the Auction tab, enter the starting price, how much each bid must go up by, and the end date. Publish it and it appears in your shop like any other product.

Do customers need an account to bid?

Yes. Bidders need to log in or register so that bids can be tracked and winners can be contacted. A login button is shown on the auction page for visitors.

How does automatic (proxy) bidding work?

A bidder enters the highest amount they are happy to pay. The plugin then bids for them in small steps, only as high as needed to stay in front, and never above their limit. Other bidders cannot see that limit.

What is a reserve price?

It is the lowest price you are willing to accept, kept secret from bidders. If the final bid is lower, the auction ends with no winner and you keep your item. You can set the plugin to relist it automatically.

What is a sealed-bid auction?

In a sealed-bid auction nobody sees the current price or anyone else’s bids. When time runs out, the highest bid wins and the winner pays exactly what they bid.

What happens when an auction ends?

The plugin picks the winner, emails them, and lets only that person add the item to the cart at the winning price. They pay with your normal checkout. If there are no bids, or the reserve is not met, nobody can buy it and you can relist it.

What if the winner doesn’t pay?

After the payment deadline you choose, the auction is marked “not paid” and you are notified. You can relist it or offer it to the next-highest bidder with one click.

Can I stop people from sniping at the last second?

Yes. Turn on last-minute protection and any bid placed in the final few minutes pushes the end time back a little, so everyone gets a fair chance to respond.

Can I let people buy an auction item right away?

Yes. Add a Buy It Now price. Shoppers can purchase at that price instead of bidding. You can have it disappear as soon as the first bid is placed.

Can I charge a fee on top of the winning bid?

Yes. Set a buyer’s fee (a percentage) for all auctions or for individual ones. It is added to the winner’s order at checkout.

Are bidder names public?

By default, names are partly hidden in the public bid list (for example “j***n”) to protect privacy. You can turn this off in the settings.

Can I block a troublemaker from bidding?

Yes. Open Auctions > Bidders, find the person, and click Ban. You can also require accounts to be a few days old before they can bid.

Will the page update by itself while people are bidding?

Yes. The price, bid list and countdown refresh automatically every few seconds, so bidders always see the latest information.

Does it work with my theme and payment methods?

It works with standard WooCommerce themes and the payment methods you already use. Winners pay through the regular checkout.

Will I lose my data if I upgrade from an older version?

No. Your existing bids and auctions are carried over automatically when you update.

Can I translate the plugin?

Yes. The plugin is ready for translation into any language.

Where can I see all the bids?

Go to Auctions > Bids. You can search, remove a bid if needed, and download everything as a spreadsheet file.
